episodes.200298: Lingering post-frontal showers near the base Cascade foothills allowed for the development of an isolated funnel cloud.
episodes.200432: During the early afternoon on Sunday, April 20, 2025 (Easter Sunday) a severe thunderstorm developed in Miller County, Missouri and moved northward through Cole County and into Callaway County. The thunderstorm produced one EF-2 tornado near New Bloomfield, MO. This occurred ahead of a line of severe thunderstorms that formed in southwest Missouri and extended northward as it moved east. The line moved into mid-Missouri during the late afternoon hours and marched into eastern Missouri. It produced 4 tornadoes in Missouri and damaging wind reports across the region.
episodes.200528: During the early evening of Sunday, April 20, 2025 (Easter Sunday) a line of severe thunderstorms responsible for multiple tornadoes and wind damage in Missouri crossed into Illinois. The line went on to produce 6 tornadoes spanning west-central, south-central, and southwest Illinois and no shortage of wind damage.
episodes.200535: High winds developed over southern Lake Michigan during the morning of April 21st with a peak wind gust to 59 mph at the Harrison Dever Crib.
episodes.201256: A warm front lifted northward through central Illinois during the afternoon of April 20th...allowing temperatures to climb well into the 70s.  As a cold front approached from the west, scattered strong to severe thunderstorms developed in the Illinois River Valley by early evening.  A few of the cells began rotating, especially as they approached the warm front along and north of the I-74 corridor.  Three tornadoes touched down...including 2 EF-1 tornadoes in Knox County and another EF-1 in Tazewell County.  Other cells produced scattered wind damage mainly west of I-55, with an isolated damaging wind gust occurring further southeast in Clay County later in the evening as the storms advanced eastward to the Indiana border.
episodes.201331: A mid-to-upper-level trough, in combination with a surface induced trough, produced periods of heavy rainfall that caused flash floods and landslides between April 19-21.
episodes.201438: A strong storm system moved through the area on Sunday April 20th, 2025.  This system brought tornadoes, damaging wind, large hail and heavy rain.  The heavy rainfall led to flooding as the area had already received heavy rainfall from storms earlier in the week. Multiple area rivers reached minor to moderate flood stage due to heavy runoff.
episodes.201602: A line of severe thunderstorms lifted north northeastward across northwest Illinois, mainly south of Interstate 80, on the evening of April 20th. This brought numerous tornadoes to the area as well as straight-line wind damage. Fourteen tornadoes occurred in northwest Illinois. 7 of them were EF-1, 5 EF-0, and 1 EF-U. The longest track tornado of the event was on the ground for 16 miles and traveled from Victoria in Knox County through Galva before lifting west of Kewanee in Henry County.
episodes.201603: A line of showers and thunderstorms developed during the early afternoon hours of April 21st over the northeastern Nebraska Panhandle. As this line of storms tracked east, it intensified over the central and northern Sandhills. Thunderstorm wind gusts up to 62 MPH were reported in southern Keya Paha and northern Brown Counties.
episodes.201876: Slow moving thunderstorms affected southeast Texas as a cold front stalled across the region.
episodes.201892: A summer-like pattern was in place across the Mid-South. The severe weather parameter space lacked adequate shear there was decent instability available. A few storms were able to tap into the available fuel and produce pulse-like hailers with a damaging wind gust or two.
episodes.202052: A line of severe thunderstorms lifted north northeastward along the Mississippi River through the Quad Cites with an area of trailing stratiform rainfall behind it. There were scattered reports of thunderstorm wind damage in the counties along the Mississippi River. A microburst occurred near West Burlington that caused damage to  a DOT Shet and broke several power poles. An NWS Storm Survey team found damage in this area consistent with wind speeds of 80 to 90 mph. In addition to the severe thunderstorms, heavy rainfall of 2 to 3 inches fell across western Johnson and southwest Linn Counties. This led to reports of flash flooding in western Cedar Rapids, Hiawatha, and Marion.
episodes.202144: A mid level trough and cold front tracking across the region caused showers and thunderstorms to develop on the afternoon of Monday April 21st. Some of the thunderstorms caused gusty winds and heavy rainfall, with at least one of the storms causing enough heavy rainfall to prompt the need for a Flash Flood Warning.
episodes.202180: The combination of sufficient tropical moisture, a washed out front, and a weak upper level disturbance allowed for slow moving thunderstorms to dump very heavy rainfall in northeast Willacy County on April 21st.  Minor flooding ensued due to rainfall rates of 2 per hour for over 2 hours.
episodes.202205: A longwave trough moved out of the Intermountain West into the Southern Plains on April 20th, which reinforced a weak cold front southeast into East Texas, Southwest Arkansas, and North Louisiana during the late afternoon through the evening into the early morning hours of the 21st. Strong heating ahead of the front as well as ample moisture enhanced instability ahead of the front, with large scale forcing sufficient along and ahead of the front/trough for the development of scattered to numerous showers and thunderstorms. While no severe weather was observed, the very moist atmospheric environment as well as the storm motion which allowed for thunderstorms to move repeatedly over the same areas did result in localized flash flooding over portions of Caddo Parish (including the city of Shreveport) in Northwest Louisiana during the evening hours, where rainfall totals ranged from 1-3 inches in a short period of time.
episodes.202260: The Black River at Black River Falls entered minor flood stage after a period of heavy rain during the afternoon on April 21st and fell below flood stage during the morning hours the next day.
episodes.202353: On the afternoon of April 21st, a cold front approaching the region began to stall over central Louisiana as upper-level support and steering flow shifted northeastward. With the front losing its dynamical push, storms developed ahead of it across the New Orleans area and became slow-moving due to the lack of steering flow. These storms produced efficient, long-duration rainfall over the city, and the urban landscape of New Orleans quickly became overwhelmed. The result was widespread flash flooding across the metro area, which persisted until the rain finally tapered off near sunset.
episodes.202354: On the afternoon of April 21st, a cold front approaching the region began to stall over central Louisiana as upper-level support and steering flow shifted northeastward. With the front losing its dynamical push, storms developed ahead of it across the New Orleans area and became slow-moving due to the lack of steering flow. As these storms moved across Lake Pontchartrain, they produced periods of gusty thunderstorm winds over the lake. The activity gradually weakened and dissipated near sunset as instability decreased.
episodes.202363: With many boundaries near the surface and a cool northwesterly flow aloft promoting shower and thunderstorm development, one landspout was observed and reported on each of April 20 and 21.
episodes.203143: Isolated severe weather developed on the afternoon and evening hours of 20th in close proximity to a warm front and associated upper level feature just north and west of Arkansas.

events.narrative: Thunderstorm winds lifted off a portion of a school's old gym roof.

This tornado continued out of Faulkner County into far northwest Lonoke County. The tornado crossed Ballard Road near the county line, just south of Ballard Hill. Most of the tornadoes path was found to be in northwest Lonoke County. This tornado crossed Highway 5 just south of the intersection of Highway 319 downing numerous trees. The tornado would then cross Highway 319 approximately 1.5 miles east of the intersection of Highway 5 and 319. Most of the damage from the tornado was tree damage, with many uprooted trees found along its path. Most of the damage to structures was found to be associated with trees falling into these structures. Within Lonoke County, the tornado was rated an EF-1 with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph.

A weak tornado touched down along Hickman Road at 7:04 PM and destroyed an outbuilding with winds estimated as strong as 85 mph. It then moved northeast through Bailey Park and produced roof damage to another outbuilding along E 2400th Street near N 2150th Ave. The tornado continued to move northeast past Golden, IL and produced roof damage to multiple outbuildings along E 2700th Street between N 2500th Ave and N 2600th Ave before dissipating just north of N 2600th Ave at 7:10 PM. The tornado was rated EF-0 with a path length of 8.17 miles and a maximum path width of 100 yards.

This tornado continued out of Lonoke County into White County. The tornado would cross Archer Road, Blakely Lane, and Gillham Road before dissipating near the community of Opal near Highway 64. The tornado removed most of the roofing material off of a couple outbuildings along its path in White County. Within White County, the tornado was rated an EF-1 with maximum estimated winds of 90 mph. The total length of the tornado was 14.1 miles and was rated an EF-1 with maximum winds of 105 mph.
The Emergency Manager reported that 5 power poles were snapped. An NWS Storm Survey found that this was caused thunderstorms straight-line wind damage.
Thunderstorm winds snapped a large tree about 5 feet above its base.
The Emergency Manager reported that a DOT Metal Building/Shed collapsed. An NWS Storm Survey found straight-line wind damage with estimated speeds of 80 to 90 MPH.
A public report of damage to a roof. The report was relayed by county 911 center. The time of the event was estimated using radar.
A trained spotter estimated wind speeds of 55 to 60 MPH.
A public report that they measured a thunderstorm wind gusts of 53 knots.
The Emergency Manager reported that a tree was blown down.
Route CC at a low water area and County Road 7060 were closed due to high water.
A public report of street flooding.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down trees in Grafton.
Thunderstorm winds downed power lines in De Soto.
A public report of a 70 MPH measured wind gust and small branches 1 inch in diameter were broken. The time of the event was estimated using radar.

An EF-1 tornado started just south of Blandinsville and tracked to NE along a 7 mile path. Tree damage was noted at numerous locations with large branches and some trees snapped. Power poles in two locations were snapped, resulting in an estimated max wind speed of 100 MPH.
Several power poles were blown down.
Thunderstorm winds downed power lines at Camilla Street and Polk Avenue near Park Hills. They also downed power lines in Desloge.
A large tree was blown down across County Highway 2 just north of its intersection with Workmans Road.

The Emergency Manager reported that apartment roof was heavily damaged with the middle section of the roof removed on both sides. In coordination with Emergency Management and reviewing photos of the damage and areas around it, this was determined to be from straight line winds with a speed of 80  mph. the time of the event was estimated using radar.
This short-lived EF-0 tornado brought tree damage, including a large uprooted tree, and a small outbuilding damaged. The peak estimated winds were 85 mph.
A trained spotter reported a large tree was blown down over the roof of a house with some siding damaged.

An EF-1 tornado occurred just to the NE of Sciota. Tree damage was found at the beginning of the 3 mile track. The tornado then strengthened and snapped power poles and eventually destroyed a farm outbuilding, with an max estimated speed of 100 MPH.
A trained spotter reported estimated 60 mph thunderstorm wind gusts.
A trained spotter reported that several shingles were lost from the roof of the house. The time of the event was estimated using radar.

A trained spotter reported that a creek was flowing out of its banks along Center Point road near Interstate 380. They also submitted photos of the flooded creek.  Rainfall reports around the area ranged from 2 to 3 inches.

Multiple deputies reported seeing a tornado from near Greenbush looking back southwest. Linking that with the garage damage by Swan Creek would make for a short-lived tornado which lines up with radar. There was no other damage reported by Warren County EMA Director. The tornado was rated EF-0 with peak estimated winds of 70 MPH.

The tornado touched down at 8:00 PM along Koch Road, southeast of Madonnaville, and moved northeast, producing minor damage to a home and an outbuilding along Rock Road. Further to the northeast along LRC Road the tornado overturned an outbuilding and caused tree damage. More tree damage and minor outbuilding roof damage occurred along JJ road as the tornado tracked northeast between Wartburg and Burksville. The tornado moved into southern Waterloo and produced minor roof damage to one of the greenhouses at Waterloo High School before turning to the east and damaging power poles along Highway 156. The power pole damage was the worst damage and winds were estimated as high as 100 mph (EF-1). The tornado dissipated shortly thereafter at 8:07 PM.The tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 7.33 miles and a maximum path width of 100 yards.
A funnel cloud was observed by the emergency manager 3 miles north-northwest of Kenyon.
Thunderstorm winds snapped multiple trees and toppled several at their base.
A trained spotter reported 60-65 mph wind gusts.
Thunderstorm winds downed power poles west of Hecker.
Broadcast media reported estimated 65 mph thunderstorm wind gusts in Waterloo. They also reported visibility near zero statute miles coinciding with the wind gust.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree over Vogel School Road just north of Floraville.

A brief and weak tornado touched down along EE Road just south of Gilmore Lake and quickly moved northeast before dissipating at the intersection of EE Road and Gilmore Lake Road at 8:13 PM. When the tornado touched down it overturned an outbuilding, and was rated at 99 mph (EF-1) at this point. Tree damage was also recorded. The tornado dissipated shortly thereafter at 8:07 PM.The tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 0.35 miles and a maximum path width of 100 yards.

A brief and weak tornado touched down on Schwab Road, southwest of Millstadt at 8:14 PM. It destroyed an outbuilding and produced tree damage along Schwab Road with winds estimated as high as 85 mph. The tornado dissipated shortly thereafter at 8:15 PM. The tornado was rated EF-0 with a path length of 0.75 miles and a maximum path width of 100 yards.
Home playground equipment was destroyed.
Thunderstorm winds downed trees crossing Illinois Route 15.

The tornado touched down on Baldwin Road at 8:25 PM, producing tree damage with winds estimated around 70 mph. The tornado then moved northeast and uprooted and snapped trees along Ridge Road. The snapped trees were the worst damage, with winds estimated as high as 93 mph. Moving northeastward, the tornado removed the roof of a grain silo along Pearidge Road before lifting at 8:26 PM just east of Pearidge Road. The tornado was rated EF-1 with a path length of 1.32 miles and a maximum path width of 75 yards.
A tree was blown onto a power line along County Road 750 North.
A 911 Dispatcher relayed a report of a tree that fell on a parked vehicle. The time of the event was estimated using radar.
Power lines were downed along AR-State Highway 34 near the intersection with US Highway 67 to the northeast of Walnut Ridge.
An NWS Storm Survey found a barn was partially damaged and some branches were down. The damage was isolated to this one property. Time of the event was estimated using radar.
An EF-0 tornado with max wind speed of 85 MPH caused damage to trees and farm outbuildings along its two mile long path.
A trained spotter reported a anemometer reading of 65 MPH with a 4 inch tree limb down.

A tornado touched down just south of Highway 167 about a mile west of Victoria at 8:39 PM CDT.  The tornado snapped 4 power poles along Highway 167, then tracked northeastward and damaged numerous trees and a few outbuildings before passing through the Galva Cemetery and crossing into the National Weather Service Quad Cities County Warning Area in Henry County at 8:49 PM CDT.

A tornado touched down along Knox Road 1525 East about 1.5 miles northeast of Altona at 8:41 PM CDT.  It destroyed a hog farm building and tossed it into a nearby outbuilding upon touchdown, then tracked northward into the National Weather Service Quad Cities County Warning Area in Henry County just east of the intersection of North Knox Road and East 1470th Street at 8:43 PM CDT.

The tornado touched down about 1.5 miles northeast of Altona in Knox County (NWS central Illinois) traveling northward and proceeded north into Henry County where it destroyed two large grain bins and tossed the debris for nearly a mile to the northeast. The tornado snapped a power pole and a large tree along US Highway 34 before dissipating along N 300 Ave where it damaged an outbuilding.
High water covered Mansfield Road just south of Barron Road beneath the railroad overpass.

A tornado touched down just southwest of the intersection of Red Shale Hill Road and Locust Road about 2 miles south of Tremont at 8:49 PM CDT.  It tracked northeastward through mainly rural areas, damaging numerous trees and a couple power poles.  The most intense part of the tornado occurred when it uprooted a 3-foot diameter tree, snapped a power pole, and peeled the top off a grain bin.  It continued northeastward, then dissipated in a field northeast of the intersection of Dee Mack Road and Cooper Road about 2 miles north of Deer Creek at 9:05 PM CDT.

The tornado touched down about a mile west of Victoria in Knox County Illinois (NWS Lincoln) traveling north northeast. It went through Galva where it snapped several trees, then it progressed northeast damaging more trees and an outbuilding along an approximately 7.2 miles path before dissipating about 3 miles west of Kewanee.
Emergency Manager reported a tree top blown off. The time of the event was estimated using radar.
An EF-U tornado with at least a 1/4 mile path was depicted by radar and a scour mark in a freshly plowed field. Corn debris was also found in the fence at this location.
Multiple streets were covered in high water throughout Shreveport, requiring several high water rescues.
A 70-foot section of a barn's wall was blown out and several 6-inch diameter tree branches were knocked down.
A brief EF-0 tornado caused damage to a door on an outbuilding. The tornado then caused branch damage before ending shortly. The peak estimated wind speed was 80 mph.

An EF-1 tornado formed to the northwest of Kewanee and tracked to the north and ended just south of Atkinson. Trees along the 7 mile path were snapped at the trunk. Some branches were downed as well. At the end of the path a structure was destroyed by max winds estimated to be 95 MPH.

A tornadic debris signature was seen on the KDVN Doppler Radar up to 2,900 ft. Corn stubble and leaves were found along the beginning of the path. As the tornado approached the Hennepin Canal, tree damage was found with snapped hardwood trees and other branches. Additional branches were found just southwest of Shady Beach. The tornado was rated as EF-1 with a peak estimated wind speed of 90 MPH.
A brief tornado caused EF-0 damage to trees with a peak estimated wind speed of 80 MPH.
The soffit was blown loose from a house.

An EF-0 tornado with maximum winds of 85 mph and a maximum width of 50 yards resulted in several trees being snapped and uprooted throughout the Cordova Cemetery, with many large branches snapped as well. As the tornado continued north, more damage to large tree branches was noted, along with an outdoor swing set and large farm irrigator damaged.
A trained spotter reported that 6 inch diameter tree branches were down. The time of the event was estimated using radar.
A large 8 to 10 inch diameter limb fell on a vehicle.

One power pole was snapped at the beginning of the path of an EF-1 tornado with peak estimate wind speed of 100 MPH. Three other power poles were replaced as well. This tornado then tracked north and led to tree damage just across county border into Whiteside County.
A tree was blown down onto Old Highway 50.
Downed powerlines at the corner of 6th St and Eastwood.
A swift water rescue was performs when a small pickup truck was swept of the road by fast flowing water. Two people were rescued safely with no injuries.

Several roads were flooded and closed around Warren including 1943 East and West, CR 4475, FM 1013  CR 4478. Multiple other roads had water covering them, but were not closed including CR 4470 and CR 1450.

events.narrative: A small landslide caused two concrete barricades to slightly sink on road PR 179 KM 10.8 in Carite.
Received pictures from the public via email of a funnel cloud near Mount Angel the morning of April 21st. MRMS indicated weak/shallow convection in the area around the time of the report.

Torrential rains fell in just a few hours across Port Mansfield between 9 AM and 1230 PM CST (10 AM and 130 PM CDT), with the cooperative observer (Harbormaster) reporting 6.83 during this time.  While the town's generally decent drainage prevented a significant flood, there was minor street flooding reported in town (water of unknown depth) during the peak of the rainfall.

The Black River at Black River Falls went into minor flood stage on April 21st during the afternoon before cresting at a height of 49.15 feet. The river stage eventually fell below flood stage during the morning hours on April 22nd.
Thunderstorm wind gust of 59 MPH measured at this location.
